published_statement: IAU 2015 B3 Table 1: '1(GM)_sun^N = 1.327 124 4 x 10^20 m^3 s^-2', nominal values 'by definition exact and ... expressed in SI units ... conversion factors only ... not as the true solar properties' (Rec. 1). Rec. 5: 'if SI masses are explicitly needed, they should be expressed in terms of (GM)_object/G, where the estimate of the Newtonian constant G should be specified in the publication (for example, the 2014 CODATA value is G = (6.67408 +- 0.00031) x 10^-11)'. Appendix A: with NSFA's G = 6.67428e-11 (CODATA 2006) 'a nominal solar mass of M_sun^N = 1.988416 x 10^30 kg'; with CODATA 2014 G, 'a solar mass of M_sun = (1.988475 +- 0.000092) x 10^30 kg'; users must state G and M_sun 'taking care that their chosen values satisfy GM_sun = (GM)_sun^N'. B3 defines NO nominal solar mass in kilograms: only the mass parameter GM is nominal.
published_hypotheses: H1 (Noting 3): G is 'one of the least precisely determined constants', the error in GM_sun is five orders of magnitude smaller -- hence GM, not M, is nominalized.

H2 (Rec. 1, Table 1 caption): nominal values are exact conversion factors chosen close to current best estimates, NOT the true solar properties; symbols without N denote actual estimates with uncertainties.
H3 (Rec. 5): any SI (kg) mass is (GM)/G with the G used stated in the publication; a kg solar mass is therefore G-dependent and carries G's uncertainty.
H4 (Sec. 4): (GM)_sun^N is the best available measurement (Petit & Luzum 2010) rounded to the precision at which TCB and TDB values agree.
H5 (Noting 1): solar mass is not secularly constant; nominal values need not track it.
H6 (App. A): chosen G and M_sun must satisfy G*M_sun = (GM)_sun^N.

A label imprecision, not a numerical error: the value is GM_N/G_2018 = 1.988409871e30 kg printed to five significant figures (truncated; rounding gives 1.98841e30).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. What B3's authors (2015-16) lacked: a consistent G. They had CODATA 2014 G = 6.67408(31)e-11 and knew the G measurements disagreed 'by several times the formal errors' (App. A). What came later: CODATA 2018 moved G to 6.67430(15)e-11 (a +3.3e-5 shift, moving a kg solar mass from 1.988475e30 to 1.988410e30) and CODATA 2022 kept it with NO new G data -- the discrepancy is not resolved (2409.03787 Sec. XVI.C.2). Also later: a measured secular GM_sun drift of -1.02e-13/yr (2201.09804). Does having it change the conclusion? No, evidence both ways: (a) B3's design anticipated exactly this missing datum -- it nominalized GM, not M, so the nominal definition is immune to G by construction; (b) the tree already uses the post-B3 G, so the 'later data' is already in its value; (c) quantities the tree reports in solar masses are G-independent when formed with GM_N, and its actual figures differ from those by -4.96e-6; kg figures (B2 = 5.4194e42 kg, EXCHANGE_RATE 1.348948e26 kg/m) carry G's 2.2e-5 (1 sigma) and at most the 5.5e-4 full spread of the 16 G measurements -- no verdict on the board depends on a figure at that precision (the refusals concern orders of magnitude, e.g. ~1e12 solar masses of NEGATIVE mass). So the lacked datum is real and still lacking, but it does not move this result as the tree uses it.
grade_evidence: Source READ (arXiv:1605.09788). The tree's M_SUN = 1.98840e30 kg is GM_N/G with the tree's own stated G (CODATA 2018 = CODATA 2022), reproduced to -4.964e-6 relative (0.22 sigma of G) by an exact-rational sympy script that also reproduces B3's own App. A kg figures. B3's substantive hypotheses are honoured: G is stated beside the mass (H3), M_SUN is used only as a reporting unit (H2). No moved datum moves a conclusion: G is unchanged 2018->2022; the GM secular drift is 1e-12; the truncation shifts build throughput and B2 by 5e-6 and the H83d match stays inside its tolerance. DISCREPANCIES RECORDED, NOT REPAIRED, NOT REFUTATIONS: (i) the tag 'IAU nominal' is imprecise -- B3 nominalizes GM only and prints no kg value equal to 1.98840e30; (ii) five-figure truncation (1.98840 vs 1.98841) breaks App. A's G*M_sun = GM_N by -4.96e-6; (iii) the tree carries four different M_SUN values across modules (1.98840 / 1.98847 / 1.98892 / 1.989 e30, spread 2.6e-4), and the H83d 2.7254e12 vs B2 2.7255e12 last-digit split is that choice alone.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if a board conclusion were shown to treat the kg solar mass as exact/definitional (G-free) where the result needs better than G's 2.2e-5, or if a verdict hinged on the fifth significant figure of a solar-mass-denominated figure (it would then need GM_N and the tree's truncation would matter). DATA-DEPENDENT if a new G determination moved CODATA's recommended value by more than the tree's reporting precision in a place where a kg figure is compared against a threshold. Nothing currently read supports either.
